skill.name: consent-registry
skill.description: Records pseudonymous consent evidence, queries lawful basis, and applies unsubscribe, complaint, bounce, restore, and erasure events through an append-only registry.
skill.summary: Manage auditable consent and suppression records without storing raw contact details.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, relative documentation links, and metadata URLs. The skill does direct agents to resolve a project root with shell substitution and invoke a Python script with an unquoted user-supplied subject identifier, creating genuine command execution risk.

remediation.issue: Dynamic project-root discovery executes Git through shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain the trusted skill root from host configuration and reject missing or unverified roots instead of invoking Git from the shell.

remediation.issue: The suppression query shows a user-supplied subject identifier as an unquoted shell argument.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers against a strict format and pass arguments through a structured process API without shell interpretation.

content.value_statement: Consent evidence and suppression status can become inconsistent across systems. This skill maintains pseudonymous, append-only records and prioritizes current suppression checks.
actual_capabilities: Records opt-in evidence with source, timestamp, lawful basis, proof references, and expected revision.
Applies immediate suppression events for unsubscribes, complaints, and hard bounces.
Queries current suppression status by replaying the authoritative consent event stream.
Restores subscriptions only after authorized, newer opt-in evidence is available.
Processes verified erasure requests while retaining a suppression tombstone.
Reviews imported consent proposals without deleting historical events.
limitations: Requires the repository runtime, schema, catalog, and registry script for authoritative mutations.
Does not send email, update an email service provider, or certify a list for sending.
Does not build audience segments or score delivery eligibility.
Accepts pseudonymous identifiers and proof references, not raw contact details.

use_cases.title: Record verified opt-in
use_cases.description: Capture lawful basis and proof references for a pseudonymous subscriber after a verified signup.

use_cases.title: Apply immediate suppression
use_cases.description: Record an unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce before another campaign eligibility check.

use_cases.title: Review consent history
use_cases.description: Check current suppression state, missing evidence, revisions, and pending proposals for an audit.

prompt_templates.title: Check suppression status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether pseudonymous subject [subject-id] is suppressed. Report the current result and relevant event reference.

prompt_templates.title: Record an opt-in
prompt_templates.prompt: Record opt-in for [subject-id] using source [source], timestamp [timestamp], basis [basis], and proof reference [proof-ref].

prompt_templates.title: Process a withdrawal
prompt_templates.prompt: Immediately suppress [subject-id] because of [unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce]. Use event reference [event-ref] and a subject-free reason code.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a restore request
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate restoring [subject-id] using new evidence [details]. Compare timestamps, authority, basis, source, and current revision before proposing any change.

output_examples.output: Suppressed: yes. The live registry replay found an accepted unsubscribe event. Do not contact this subject.

output_examples.input: Record a new opt-in with no lawful basis reference.
output_examples.output: The opt-in was not recorded. Lawful basis remains unknown, and a valid basis or proof reference is required.

output_examples.input: Restore a subject using proof older than the withdrawal.
output_examples.output: Restore denied. The submitted evidence predates the withdrawal and cannot clear the current suppression state.

best_practices: Use only pseudonymous subject identifiers and minimum opaque proof references.
Query the live event stream before every eligibility or send decision.
Record withdrawals immediately and require fresh authorized evidence for restoration.
anti_patterns: Do not store email addresses, names, phone numbers, or raw identifiers in registry events.
Do not infer consent from imports, engagement, similarity, or missing evidence.
Do not manually edit projections or clear suppression without an authorized restore event.

faq.question: Does this skill send email?
faq.answer: No. It records consent state and suppression events. Sending and provider synchronization are separate operations.

faq.question: Can it store email addresses?
faq.answer: No. Use pseudonymous subject identifiers and opaque proof references. Raw contact details are outside this skill.

faq.question: What events cause immediate suppression?
faq.answer: An unsubscribe, complaint, or hard bounce should create an immediate deny-only suppression event.

faq.question: Can old opt-in evidence restore a subscription?
faq.answer: No. Restore evidence must be trusted, authorized, and strictly newer than the withdrawal or erasure.

faq.question: Which record is authoritative?
faq.answer: The append-only consent event stream and replay query are authoritative. Human-readable projections are caches.

faq.question: Can a standalone installation change canonical state?
faq.answer: No. Without the verified runtime, schema, catalog, and host capabilities, it can only prepare a proposal or handoff.
